name: suite-tool-followups-provenance
body:
Provenance: these are follow-ups discovered during the `suite-query-error-guard` cycle. The empty-target gap (fix A) specifically blocked resolving feedback-1 there — with no way to clear a stale task's target, the authoring session could not make the task honest and had to delete it instead. Fixes B and C are small drift/hygiene defects found in the same pass: the shared lib carried a second copy of the missing-DB literal, and the installer's scaffolded `@opencode-ai/plugin` pin (1.18.10) had fallen behind the suite manifest's (1.18.20). Scope is exactly A/B/C — no scanner or TypeScript-identity work (that is the separate `scanner-optimisation` change-set).

Merge-drift correction: the first merge attempt's main rebuild failed with `spec drift: code FQN .../apg/.worktrees/suite-tool-followups/opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_add.ts is gone from the scanned graph`. `solution.component.suite-tool-followups` had been anchored with two absolute File-path FQNs rooted at this worktree — the `apg_plan_add.ts` tool file and `src/main.rs` — which are checkout-dependent: on `main` those files resolve to different absolute paths, so the anchor is drift. Correction: removed both File-path anchors, leaving exactly the two checkout-independent Function anchors that the implementing tasks genuinely change (`apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.runCli` and `apg.plan_cmd.plan_update`), rewrote the component body's anchoring statement, and added `global.constraint.checkout-independent-code-anchors`. Law: a durable `implemented-by` anchor must be a checkout-independent code FQN (Module/Struct/Function); never an absolute File path. This is the same root cause as `global.constraint.checkout-independent-module-identity` (a checkout-directory identity entering the durable spec), applied to File-path anchors.
